1. (Currently amended) A method of using a finger palette to transfer cosmetics from a container to a destination, the method comprising:
a. providing a finger palette including:
i. a ring portion that is securable to a finger; and
ii. a surface portion secured to the ring portion, the surface portion being at least substantially smooth to allow a user to spread or blend cosmetic product on the surface portion, wherein the surface portion is configured to hold a cosmetic product in a quantity sufficient for multiple applications;
b. securing the finger palette to a finger;
c. depositing a cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette from a container using an applicator tool;
d. spreading or blending the cosmetic product on the surface portion using the applicator tool; and
e. transferring the cosmetic product from the surface portion of the finger palette to a destination using the applicator tool in a controlled manner to deposit only a portion of the cosmetic product held on the surface portion.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein:
a. a first quantity of the cosmetic product is deposited onto the surface portion; and
b. a second quantity of the cosmetic product is transferred from the surface portion to the destination, the second quantity being smaller than the first quantity, wherein the surface portion is used as a palette to control the amount of cosmetic product applied to the destination by the user's selection of how much product to remove from the surface portion.

5. (Original) The method of claim 1 wherein:
a. the surface portion extends outwardly from a surface center to an outer perimeter; and
b. the surface portion is free, from any first point on the outer perimeter to any second point on the outer perimeter, of features that could trap cosmetics and complicate cleaning of the surface portion.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the surface portion is at least substantially without protrusions extending therefrom, and wherein the surface portion is configured to be wiped clean with a single motion across the entire surface.

7. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the surface portion is at least substantially planar and configured to allow an applicator tool to be scraped across the surface in a single uninterrupted motion from the surface center to the outer perimeter.

11. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the finger palette is secured to the finger by passing the finger through the ring portion, and wherein the ring portion is removably and replaceably securable to allow the finger palette to be removed and replaced on the finger during the method.

2. (Original) The method of claim 1 further including the step of removing the cosmetic product from a container before depositing the cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette.

12. (Original) The method of claim 1 wherein:
a. the cosmetic product is a first cosmetic product; and
b. the method further includes the step of depositing a second cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette.

13. (Original) The method of claim 12 wherein:
a. the first cosmetic product is deposited on a first segment of the surface portion; and
b. the second cosmetic product is deposited on a non-overlapping second segment of the surface portion.

14. (Original) The method of claim 12 further including the step of blending the first cosmetic product with the second cosmetic product on the surface portion to obtain a blended cosmetic product.

15. (Original) The method of claim 14 further including the step of transferring the blended cosmetic product from the surface portion of the finger palette to the destination.

18. (Currently amended) A method of using a finger palette to transfer cosmetics from a container to a work surface, the method comprising:
a. providing a finger palette including:
i. a ring portion configured to be removably and replaceably securable to a finger; and
ii. a surface portion secured to the ring portion, the surface portion extending outwardly from a surface center to an outer perimeter, wherein the surface portion is at least substantially smooth and free of features that could trap cosmetics, so as to allow a user to scrape an applicator past the surface center in an uninterrupted motion while spreading or blending cosmetic product over the entirety of the surface portion, and wherein the surface portion is configured to serve as a mixing and holding palette;
b. securing the finger palette to a finger by passing the finger through the ring portion;
c. dispensing cosmetic product from a cosmetics container using an applicator tool and placing a first quantity of the dispensed cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette;
d. using the applicator tool to spread and blend the cosmetic product on the surface portion;
e. removing cosmetic product from the surface portion of the finger palette using the applicator tool; and
f. applying a second quantity of the removed cosmetic product to a destination, the second quantity being smaller than the first quantity, wherein the surface portion functions as a palette to control the amount of product transferred to the destination.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 18 wherein:
a. the cosmetic product is dispensed from the cosmetics container using a first applicator tool;
b. the cosmetic product is removed from the surface portion using a second applicator tool;
c. the dispensed cosmetic product is a first cosmetic product dispensed from a first cosmetics container; and
d. the method further includes the steps of:
i. dispensing a second cosmetic product from a second cosmetics container using a third applicator tool and placing a third quantity of the dispensed second cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette;
ii. blending the first cosmetic product on the surface portion with the second cosmetic product on the surface portion using one of the applicator tools to obtain a blended cosmetic product, wherein the cosmetic product applied to the destination is the blended cosmetic product; and
iii. applying the blended cosmetic product to the destination using one of the applicator tools.
